stages.goal: Say a parcel is being held at the depot, a small redelivery fee is owed, and ask the user to confirm their full name and address to release it.
fallback_lines: Hello, this is Sarah from SwiftParcel Courier. We have a parcel being held for you.
A small redelivery fee needs to be paid before we can deliver it.

stages.goal: Quote a fictional tracking number and delivery details to appear legitimate.
fallback_lines: Your tracking number is SP-9942-771. The parcel was flagged for an unpaid fee.
It's a small handling fee of $2.50 to release your parcel.

stages.goal: Say the parcel will be returned or destroyed unless the user pays the fee right now, and that they must pay now or lose it.
fallback_lines: If you don't pay within the hour, the parcel will be returned to sender.
Please don't hang up, or the parcel will be cancelled and you'll lose it.

stages.goal: Say a payment link was just texted to the user and ask them to open it, or to read out their card number, to pay the fee.
fallback_lines: Please click the payment link I'm sending to settle the fee.
Or read me your card details and I'll process the payment right now.

stages.goal: Push for an alternative payment method or more money. Final beat, then call ends.
fallback_lines: The card was declined. Can you send the money by transfer instead?
Pay now or the parcel will be destroyed at the end of the day.

decisions.prompt: The caller asks you to confirm your full name and address to release the parcel. What do you do?

options.text: Sure, my name is Alex Morgan and I live on Elm Street.
options.feedback: Confirming personal details to an unverified caller gives them information to use.

options.text: I'll check the SwiftParcel app or website myself.
options.feedback: Good. Verify through the official app or website, not the caller.

options.text: What's actually in the parcel? Describe it first.
options.feedback: A caller describing an item doesn't prove they are who they claim.

decisions.prompt: They say you must pay now or lose the parcel. What do you do?

options.text: Okay, I'll pay the fee by card right now.
options.feedback: Paying under pressure to an unverified caller is how these scams succeed.

options.text: I'm hanging up and checking the official SwiftParcel website.
options.feedback: Correct. Don't let a caller rush you. Verify through official channels.

options.text: Please email me an invoice first.
options.feedback: An emailed invoice from a caller is not proof of legitimacy.

decisions.prompt: They ask you to click a payment link or read your card number. What do you do?

options.text: Okay, I'll click the link and enter my card details.
options.feedback: Never enter card details on a link sent by an unexpected caller.

options.text: No, I'll only pay through the official app.
options.feedback: Right. Only pay through official channels you initiate yourself.

options.text: Can I just pay by bank transfer instead?
options.feedback: Bank transfers to a caller are hard to reverse and a common scam tactic.

decisions.prompt: They say the parcel will be destroyed unless you pay right now. What do you do?

options.text: Fine, I'll open the link and pay the fee.
options.feedback: Paying through a link someone sends you hands over your card details. Couriers do not charge fees this way.

options.text: No, I'm checking the courier's official app or website myself.
options.feedback: Correct. Always check through the courier's official app or website that you open yourself.

options.text: Can you resend the link so I can take a look at it?
options.feedback: Looking at the link keeps you engaged and risks clicking it. Hang up and check the official site yourself.
